question: Does a learned joint future distribution better preserve the combinations and persistence that define multivariate disturbance?
backbone: Shared HNE state/context GRU32, personal-reference node encoder, context FiLM and indicator attention; same weights and operators across channels and datasets
input_transform: asinh of normalized state/context histories and node descriptors; state/context units remain fixed; descriptor scalers fit on training participants
future: seven normalized state observations at d+2 through d+8; never enter the predictor input
value_distribution: Gaussian in asinh coordinates, covariance diagonal variance plus rank4 factors shared across all future days and state variables; rank0 control
observation_distribution: Bernoulli observation probabilities per future day/variable, conditionally independent of trajectory values given history
loss: equal-person average of observed-coordinate Gaussian NLL including inverse-transform Jacobian, plus Bernoulli observation NLL; no event-label loss
risk: Monte Carlo evaluation of unchanged personal-reference amplitude, displacement, persistence and family rules; probability conditional on a resolved future label
selection: minimum equal-person validation joint loss; fixed architecture, no test-based choice
evaluation: original five participant-disjoint development folds; all seeds and both covariance conditions reported; exposed external tests are not reclassified as confirmation
scope: joint-density learning itself has prior art; this experiment tests translating coherent future trajectories and observation availability through a sustained-disturbance operator
